- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# RED test for F3: `./hsim run <elf> --mode csr|pc --kanata FILE`.
3	#
4	# Produces a kanata pipeline log restricted to the ROI region of the
5	# hybrid run. csr-mode auto-derives ROI bounds from the resume PC and
6	# the unique `csrwi 0x7C0,1` PC. pc-mode honors --pc-start/--pc-end.
7	
8	set -uo pipefail
9	
10	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
11	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
12	HSIM="$ROOT/hsim"
13	
14	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
15	
16	[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"
17	
18	# Same convention as tests/lib/paths.sh: fall back to ./config.env when
19	# the toolchain isn't already on the env, so --objdump probing works
20	# without requiring `source ./setup.sh` first.
21	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
22	  . "$ROOT/config.env"
23	fi
24	
25	cd "$ROOT"
26	
27	TMPDIR_ROOT=$(mktemp -d -t hsim-kanata-XXXXXX)
28	trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR_ROOT"' EXIT
29	
30	# 1. --help advertises --kanata and --objdump on the run subcommand.
31	out=$("$HSIM" run --help 2>&1) || fail "run --help exit nonzero: $out"
32	echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--kanata"  || fail "run --help missing --kanata:\n$out"
33	echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--objdump" || fail "run --help missing --objdump:\n$out"
34	ok "run --help lists --kanata and --objdump"
35	
36	# 2. --kanata with --mode icount -> rc=2 (the kanata-roi path only supports
37	#    csr/pc).
38	set +e
39	out=$("$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode icount \
40	       --kanata "$TMPDIR_ROOT/x.kanata" 2>&1); rc=$?
41	set -e
42	[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "--kanata with icount should rc=2, got $rc:\n$out"
43	echo "$out" | grep -qi "kanata" || fail "icount rejection should mention kanata:\n$out"
44	ok "--kanata + --mode icount rejected (rc=2)"
45	
46	# 3. csr-mode smoke: kanata file is created, non-empty, has Kanata header.
47	KFILE="$TMPDIR_ROOT/csr.kanata"
48	SMOKE_TIMEOUT=60
49	set +e
50	out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
51	        --mode csr --kanata "$KFILE" 2>&1); rc=$?
52	set -e
53	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "csr-mode kanata run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
54	[ -s "$KFILE" ] || fail "csr-mode: kanata file not created or empty: $KFILE"
55	head -1 "$KFILE" | grep -q "^Kanata" \
56	  || fail "csr-mode: kanata file missing 'Kanata' header (first line):\n$(head -2 "$KFILE")"
57	# ROI window must have at least one fetched insn (I record) and one
58	# retired insn (R record). Both should appear after the LoopGate opens.
59	grep -q "^I	" "$KFILE" \
60	  || fail "csr-mode: kanata file has no I (start_insn) records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE")"
61	grep -q "^R	" "$KFILE" \
62	  || fail "csr-mode: kanata file has no R (retire_insn) records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE")"
63	ok "csr-mode --kanata produces a valid kanata trace"
64	
65	# 4. csr-mode with --objdump: a load-line shows the disassembly. This
66	#    proves the OBJDUMP_FILE env reached vsim via e2e.sh.
67	DUMP="$TMPDIR_ROOT/rt_c_hello.S"
68	OBJDUMP_TOOL="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
69	OBJDUMP_TOOL="${OBJDUMP_TOOL:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
70	if ! command -v "$OBJDUMP_TOOL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
71	  echo "[skip] objdump not found ($OBJDUMP_TOOL); skipping --objdump check"
72	else
73	  "$OBJDUMP_TOOL" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf > "$DUMP" \
74	    || fail "objdump -d failed for rt_c_hello.elf"
75	  KFILE2="$TMPDIR_ROOT/csr-dump.kanata"
76	  set +e
77	  out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
78	          --mode csr --kanata "$KFILE2" --objdump "$DUMP" 2>&1); rc=$?
79	  set -e
80	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "csr+objdump run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
81	  # With objdump, L records should embed the asm text after the PC.
82	  # Example: "L\t1\t0\t0x800000ec: csrwi  0x7c0,1"
83	  grep -E "^L\b.*0x[0-9a-f]+: [a-z]" "$KFILE2" >/dev/null \
84	    || fail "csr+objdump: no L record with disassembly text:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE2")"
85	  ok "csr-mode --kanata --objdump embeds disassembly"
86	fi
87	
88	# 5. pc-mode smoke: explicit --pc-start/--pc-end. ROI bounds come from
89	#    objdump; skip if objdump is unavailable.
90	if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_TOOL:-}" ] && command -v "$OBJDUMP_TOOL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
91	  # Match on the raw 32-bit insn encoding (toolchains print 0x7C0 as
92	  # either "0x7c0" or the Andes name "milmb"; the encoding is stable).
93	  #   csrwi 0x7C0, 0 -> 0x7c005073
94	  #   csrwi 0x7C0, 1 -> 0x7c00d073
95	  # `awk ... exit` closes its stdin early; with pipefail set, objdump
96	  # gets SIGPIPE (141) and kills the script under errexit. Use NR-guard
97	  # so awk drains the producer, no SIGPIPE.
98	  ENTER=$("$OBJDUMP_TOOL" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
99	            | awk 'matched==0 && /7c005073/{gsub(":","",$1); print $1; matched=1}')
100	  EXIT=$("$OBJDUMP_TOOL" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
101	            | awk 'matched==0 && /7c00d073/{gsub(":","",$1); print $1; matched=1}')
102	  if [ -n "${ENTER:-}" ] && [ -n "${EXIT:-}" ]; then
103	    KFILE3="$TMPDIR_ROOT/pc.kanata"
104	    set +e
105	    out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
106	            --mode pc --pc-start "0x$ENTER" --pc-end "0x$EXIT" \
107	            --kanata "$KFILE3" 2>&1); rc=$?
108	    set -e
109	    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc-mode kanata run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
110	    [ -s "$KFILE3" ] || fail "pc-mode: kanata file not created or empty"
111	    head -1 "$KFILE3" | grep -q "^Kanata" \
112	      || fail "pc-mode: missing Kanata header"
113	    grep -q "^I	" "$KFILE3" \
114	      || fail "pc-mode: no I records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE3")"
115	    ok "pc-mode --kanata produces a valid kanata trace"
116	  else
117	    echo "[skip] could not extract csrwi 0x7c0 markers from rt_c_hello"
118	  fi
119	fi
120	
121	echo "PASS test_hsim_kanata"
122

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end roundtrip harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim -> QEMU 2.
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
13	#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
14	#   ROI_START       pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol
15	#                   in $VSIM_ELF.
16	#   ROI_END         pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-out PC, same forms.
17	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
18	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
19	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
20	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
25	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
26	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
27	
28	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
29	EXPECT_RC="${EXPECT_RC:-0}"
30	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
31	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"
32	
33	hybrid_resolve_paths
34	
35	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
36	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
37	
38	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
39	  csr) ;;
40	  pc)
41	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
42	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
43	      exit 77
44	    fi
45	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
46	    # ROI_START / ROI_END (env, both required) name the two switch PCs:
47	    # each is a 0x address or a symbol in $VSIM_ELF.
48	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
49	    ;;
50	  *)
51	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
52	    exit 1
53	    ;;
54	esac
55	
56	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
57	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
58	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
59	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
60	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
61	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
62	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
63	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
64	
65	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
66	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
67	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
68	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
69	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
70	fi
71	
72	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
73	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
74	# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
75	VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
76	if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
77	  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
78	  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
79	    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
80	  fi
81	fi
82	
83	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
84	set +e
85	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
86	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
87	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
88	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
89	  -nographic \
90	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
91	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
92	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" >/dev/null 2>&1
93	QEMU1_RC=$?
94	set -e
95	
96	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
97	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
98	  exit 1
99	fi
100	
101	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
102	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
103	  exit 1
104	fi
105	
106	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain + spawn QEMU 2"
107	set +e
108	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
109	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
110	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
111	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
112	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
113	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \

Perfect! Now I have enough information. Let me compile my findings:

## HACKY PATTERNS REVIEW

**verilator/src/main.cpp:425–440 and :522–524 - Double validation of kanata-roi preconditions**

The validation block at lines 425–440 checks:
- `args.kanata_file.empty()` 
- `loop_gate` (set)
- `args.clarity_file` (!empty)
- `args.hybrid_icount` (set)
- `args.resume_from_qemu.empty()`

Then `enable_kanata_roi()` (simulator.hpp:557–563) re-checks:
- `!hybrid_input_state_` (which maps to `args.resume_from_qemu.empty()`)
- `!hybrid_handoff_` (which maps to `args.hybrid_icount` + trigger mode)

These are redundant. Main.cpp validates the CLI args upfront, then the method validates internal state. Either move all checks to main.cpp, or hoist them into a separate `validate_kanata_roi_args()` helper called by both.

**Suggested fix:** Consolidate into a single validation function in simulator.hpp that main.cpp calls after apply_resume_from_qemu, eliminating the duplicate checks in main.cpp.

---

**verilator/src/hybrid/kanata_roi.hpp:25–31 and kanata_logger.hpp:22–28 - Identical struct definitions**

`RoiKanataGate` (kanata_roi.hpp) and `kanata::LoopGate` (kanata_logger.hpp) have identical layouts (all uint64_t: start_pc, end_pc, skip_iters, record_iters). There's a constructor-style aggregate initialization in kanata_roi.hpp:55 (`RoiKanataGate{...}`) that then gets copied to `kanata::LoopGate{...}` in simulator.hpp:570.

**Suggested fix:** Alias `RoiKanataGate` to `kanata::LoopGate`, or return `kanata::LoopGate` directly from `derive_roi_kanata_gate()`. Eliminates the copy and the duplicate struct.

---

**tests/hsim/test_hsim_kanata.sh:98–101 - Duplicate objdump invocations with magic number alternation**

Lines 98–99 invoke `objdump -d` to extract ENTER (encoding `7c005073`). Lines 100–101 invoke it again to extract EXIT (encoding `7c00d073`). Both extract from the same file. The encoding magic numbers lack a central definition.

**Suggested fix:** Read objdump once into a temp file, then grep both patterns. Or define `ENTER_ENCODING=7c005073` and `EXIT_ENCODING=7c00d073` as constants at the top of the test, reducing brittleness.

---

**tests/e2e.sh:65–70 vs :75–81 - Asymmetric array-building patterns**

`VSIM_TRIG_ARGS` is built with conditional `PLUGIN_ARGS` modifications (line 68 appends `enter_pc=` only in pc mode), but `VSIM_KANATA_ARGS` unconditionally includes `--kanata-roi` (line 77) without gating on mode. The parallel structure is visually similar but has different preconditions: KANATA_FILE gates on `args.kanata` (csr/pc modes only), while PLUGIN_ARGS gates on `TRIGGER_MODE == pc`. This invites copy-paste errors.

**Suggested fix:** Add explicit comments documenting why each array's conditionals differ, or restructure so both follow the same pattern (e.g., both check mode explicitly).

---

**verilator/src/hybrid/kanata_roi.hpp:1–10 comment - Narrates WHAT instead of non-obvious WHY**

The comment describes the logic (start_pc = resume PC, end_pc = explicit or scanned EXIT) but doesn't explain *why* the csr-mode scan throws on 0 or >1 exits. The error message hints (line 44: "use --mode pc"), but a top-level comment should clarify: hybrid ROI requires a *single* deterministic exit point for reproducibility; csr-mode enforces this via the magic CSR write, pc-mode allows override for flexibility.

**Suggested fix:** Replace WHAT description with a brief WHY: "Ensures a single, reproducible ROI window: csr-mode auto-derives end_pc from the ELF's unique exit marker; pc-mode allows explicit override."

---

**SUMMARY:** Two structural issues (double validation, duplicate struct) and three maintainability issues (duplicate tool invocations, asymmetric conditionals, unclear comments). None affect correctness in the happy path, but all reduce clarity and invite future bugs.
